clue.text: Upset on sea, wretched mostly — so it is!

definitions.text: Upset on sea, wretched mostly — so it is!

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the assembled letters are turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: RE means on or about, as in a letter heading
the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its final letter, keeping most of it

parts.note: lame means feeble or wretched, as a lame excuse

explanation.surface: Someone feeling dreadful on a boat trip groans that they are indeed upset and wretched.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, MED and LAM (LAME without its last letter) give REMEDLAM; 'Upset' turns it over to give MAL DE MER. The whole clue also describes the condition, hence the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Mal de mer is French for seasickness, the queasy upset felt on a boat at sea.

clue.text: Down payment raised in company owned by 26's rival in 9

parts.note: down means sad, as does blue

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word is read upwards, so it is turned round

parts.note: a giro is a payment by bank transfer, or a British state benefit cheque
taken as written

explanation.surface: A deposit on a purchase, linked oddly to some company owned by a business rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 is ELON MUSK and 9 is SPACE TOURISM; his rival there is Jeff Bezos. 'Down payment' looks like one phrase but splits into a mood and a payment.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue Origin is the rocket firm founded and owned by Jeff Bezos, Musk's competitor in selling flights to space.

clue.text: See 2
See 9
Country Spain hit in India

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)
to swat is to hit sharply
taken as written
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A sporting report: a country's team, Spain, struck a blow while playing in India.
explanation.definitionFit: Eswatini, formerly Swaziland, is a small kingdom in southern Africa.

clue.text: Constable country, with criminal stealing two articles?

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
two copies of the indefinite article A

explanation.surface: A police constable patrols his country beat, where a criminal is pinching a couple of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constable' suggests a policeman, which fits 'criminal' and 'stealing'; it is John Constable, the painter.
explanation.definitionFit: The painter John Constable worked in Suffolk's Stour valley, part of the eastern English region still nicknamed Constable Country.

clue.text: Flipping old story ending in wedding — that's sweet

indicators.note: flipping turns the letters over, so in a down clue they read upwards

parts.note: a tale is a story

indicators.note: ending in picks the last letter of the word that follows

parts.note: its last letter is G

explanation.surface: A tired anecdote that ends at a wedding is called sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelato is Italian ice cream, a dessert or sweet in British usage.

clue.text: Big jumper everyone in conflict loves

indicators.note: in means the word for everyone sits inside the word for conflict

parts.note: war is armed conflict
all means everyone
love is zero in tennis, and zero looks like O, so two loves give OO

explanation.surface: A lover not fighter: someone who adores everyone even in wartime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big jumper' could be a large sweater, called a jumper in Britain; here it is an animal that jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: A wallaroo is a large kangaroo-like marsupial of Australia that moves by hopping.

clue.text: Flights of fancy supremacist leader in organisation conjured up

indicators.note: conjured up suggests magicking something new out of the letters, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: leader in picks the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: its first letter is O

explanation.surface: A fanciful idea dreamt up by the head of some supremacist group.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying passengers rocketed briefly into orbit for pleasure take expensive, fanciful flights rather than journeys with a practical purpose.

clue.text: Python having a snooze?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Eric ..., a member of the Monty Python comedy team
second meaning: inactive, doing nothing, as when dozing

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a snake asleep; one meaning is a comedian's surname, the other an adjective for inactivity.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Idle was one of the Monty Python troupe, and someone dozing is inactive, not working.

clue.text: Harry: kid returning with barrel, having trapped a monster

indicators.note: returning means the words for harry and kid are read backwards together

parts.note: to harry is to pester or nag
to kid is to tease, or rag

indicators.note: having trapped means the barrel word holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: a tun is a large cask or barrel

explanation.surface: Harry, a naughty child, comes back with a barrel in which he has caught a monster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a boy's name but is the verb meaning to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: Monster used as an adjective means huge, like gargantuan, from Rabelais's giant Gargantua.

clue.text: Powerful woman, concern of 26's rival in 9?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a strong, warlike woman, after the female warriors of Greek legend
second meaning: the business founded by Jeff Bezos, Musk's competitor in space tourism

explanation.walkthrough: 26 is ELON MUSK and 9 is SPACE TOURISM, where his rival is Jeff Bezos of Blue Origin; 'concern' here means a business.
explanation.definitionFit: Amazons were mythical warrior women, and Amazon is the online retail company Bezos built.

clue.text: Lazy as grazers munching top of bush, variegated plant

indicators.note: lazy suggests something slack and sloppily arranged, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, top of picks the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: its first letter is B

explanation.surface: Idle cattle and sheep chewing the top of a shrub that has striped leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'munching' tells you the B goes in among the grazers' letters before 'Lazy' shuffles the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Zebra grass is an ornamental miscanthus whose leaves carry horizontal yellow bands, a variegated garden grass.

clue.text: Battle site a shade outside capital in Oman, inducement required to defend it

indicators.note: the inducement word must guard what has been built so far, so it goes around it

parts.note: a sop is something given to pacify or win someone over

indicators.note: outside means the shade word goes around the next letter

parts.note: pink is a shade of colour

indicators.note: capital in means the first letter, the capital, of the word that follows

parts.note: its first letter is O

explanation.surface: A battlefield description: a shady spot near Muscat, defended with the help of a bribe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital in Oman' tempts you towards Muscat, but only the capital letter is wanted. 'it' points at everything built so far, which the inducement surrounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Spion Kop is the hill in South Africa where British troops suffered a heavy defeat in the Boer War in 1900.

clue.text: Language student again taken in by a rogue

indicators.note: taken in by means the word for again is held inside the rogue word

parts.note: a rat is a scoundrel or rogue
bis means twice or again, used in music for a repeat

explanation.surface: A student repeating a course is duped by a con man.
explanation.definitionFit: An Arabist is a scholar who studies the Arabic language and culture.

clue.text: Shimmering bridge shown after opening of gate

parts.note: to span is to bridge, as a bridge spans a river

indicators.note: after means the word for shown comes after the gate letter
opening of picks the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: its first letter is G
led means showed the way, as in shown to a seat

explanation.surface: A glittering bridge comes into view once the gate is opened.
explanation.definitionFit: Spangled means decorated with spangles, small glittering ornaments, so it sparkles or glitters.

clue.text: Wrinkly earthman is going after final wishes — did he boldly go?

indicators.note: going after means the shuffled letters come after the will

parts.note: a will sets out a person's final wishes

indicators.note: wrinkly suggests something crumpled out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An aged Earth-dweller, after making his will, wonders if he really went where no man has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrinkly' looks like an adjective for the old earthman; it is the anagram signal. 'Boldly go' echoes the Star Trek opening.
explanation.definitionFit: The actor who played Captain Kirk, whose mission was 'to boldly go', really flew into space in 2021 aged ninety.

clue.text: Local river south of a lake, did you say?

indicators.note: in a down clue, south of means the river comes below, so after, the other letters

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake
eh? is what you say when asking someone to repeat themselves
the Ouse is a river in England

explanation.surface: Someone asks for directions: a river lies south of a lake, did you say?
explanation.walkthrough: 'did you say' suggests a homophone, but here it simply gives EH. In Britain your 'local' is the pub you usually drink at.
explanation.definitionFit: An alehouse is a pub, and a regular's nearest pub is called the local.

clue.text: See 17
A criminal back into drugs, tried

indicators.note: into means the earlier pieces go inside the word for drugs

parts.note: hash is hashish, a cannabis drug

indicators.note: back means the word for criminal is read in reverse

parts.note: bad means wicked or criminal

explanation.surface: A crook who has gone back to using drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed criminal comes after A, and that pair goes into the drugs word just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a bash is an informal phrase for attempting something, so had a bash means had a go at it.

clue.text: A second US president arising, primitive life form

parts.note: mo is a short while, a second

indicators.note: in a down clue, arising means the word reads upwards, so it is reversed

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, the US president

explanation.surface: A second American president rising up, seen as something primitive.
explanation.definitionFit: An amoeba is a single-celled organism, a simple and early type of living creature.

clue.text: 26's business, better returns in it

indicators.note: in means the reversed word sits inside the word for it

parts.note: it is a coy word for sex appeal or sex

indicators.note: returns means the word for better is read backwards

parts.note: to cap is to better or outdo

explanation.surface: A firm's profits improve when there is sex involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 is ELON MUSK. 'It' meaning sex appeal is an old euphemism.
explanation.definitionFit: SpaceX is the rocket company Elon Musk founded, his space-launch enterprise.

clue.text: I had put in crooked nose, laterally

indicators.note: put in means the contracted words go inside the rearranged letters
crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone with a bent nose, seen from the side in profile.
explanation.walkthrough: The contraction lands between the first letter and the rest of the shuffled nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Side-on means viewed or placed from the side, sideways, which is what laterally means.

clue.text: Company considered stocking hairpiece marked with parallel folds

indicators.note: stocking means holding something inside, so the word for considered contains the hairpiece

parts.note: rated means judged or considered
rug is slang for a wig or hairpiece

explanation.surface: A firm judged to be selling wigs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stocking' looks like hosiery or a shop stocking goods; it signals containment.
explanation.definitionFit: Corrugated iron and cardboard are shaped into a series of alternating ridges and grooves.

clue.text: Ring children's character back

indicators.note: back means the character's name is read in reverse

parts.note: Pooh is Winnie-the-Pooh, the bear of A. A. Milne's children's books

explanation.surface: A ring-shaped toy brings back a favourite storybook character.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoop is a circular band, a ring of wood or metal.

clue.text: It's a song, that man said

indicators.note: said means the word sounds like the one spoken, not spelt

parts.note: him is that man as an object pronoun

explanation.surface: Someone identifies a tune, adding that a man said so.
explanation.definitionFit: A hymn is a religious song of praise, sung in church.

clue.text: Moisten first of tissues that's poked into bottom

indicators.note: poked into means the letter is pushed inside the bottom word

parts.note: the base is the bottom of something

indicators.note: first of picks the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: its first letter is T

explanation.surface: Wipes being pushed into someone's bottom to wet it, as with a baby.
explanation.definitionFit: To baste is to moisten roasting meat with its fat or juices.

clue.text: Rich man investing amount of money in country house after retirement

indicators.note: retirement is going back, so the built letters are read in reverse
investing means putting the money word inside the house word

parts.note: Knole is a large country house in Kent, England
a sum is an amount of money

explanation.surface: A wealthy man puts money into a country estate once he has retired.
explanation.walkthrough: Knole, a great house in Kent, is not widely known outside Britain. 'retirement' signals going back, so the whole construction is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Elon Musk, founder of Tesla and SpaceX, has been ranked the world's wealthiest person.
